label: Bible Study
prompt: And he saith unto them, Be not affrighted: Ye seek Jesus of Nazareth, which was crucified: he is _____; he is not here: behold the place where they laid him.
verse: And he saith unto them, Be not affrighted: Ye seek Jesus of Nazareth, which was crucified: he is risen; he is not here: behold the place where they laid him.
note: The young man in white at the tomb delivers the first Easter announcement — come see the empty place.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: Behold, I send an Angel before thee, to keep thee in the way, and to bring thee into the place which I have _____.
verse: Behold, I send an Angel before thee, to keep thee in the way, and to bring thee into the place which I have prepared.
note: God sends an Angel ahead to guard the road — and the destination is already prepared.

label: Sunday School
prompt: Then was the iron, the clay, the brass, the silver, and the gold, broken to pieces together, and became like the _____ of the summer threshingfloors; and the wind carried them away, that no place was found for them: and the stone that smote the image became a great mountain, and filled the whole earth.
verse: Then was the iron, the clay, the brass, the silver, and the gold, broken to pieces together, and became like the chaff of the summer threshingfloors; and the wind carried them away, that no place was found for them: and the stone that smote the image became a great mountain, and filled the whole earth.
note: A stone cut without hands smashed the great statue into chaff and grew into a mountain that filled the earth.

label: Deep Water
prompt: Wherefore, my beloved brethren, let every man be _____ to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath:
verse: Wherefore, my beloved brethren, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath:
note: James's three-part rule for every argument: fast ears, slow mouth, slower temper.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: Yet all this _____ me nothing, so long as I see Mordecai the Jew sitting at the king's gate.
verse: Yet all this availeth me nothing, so long as I see Mordecai the Jew sitting at the king's gate.
note: Haman had riches, sons, and royal favour, yet it all 'availeth me nothing' while Mordecai sat at the gate. Envy spoils the feast.
